Tuga A8 vs Tuga W8

For anyone set on an 8 inch rugged tablet and undecided between Android and Windows. The short answer: buy the Tuga A8 and keep £250, unless a program you rely on only runs on a Windows PC, in which case the Tuga W8 is the one.

Verdict

The short answer

Software decides this one. The Tuga A8 costs £379 and the Tuga W8 costs £629, a gap of £250 for two tablets with the same 8 inch screen size, the same 1280 x 800 resolution, 128GB of storage, IP67 sealing, 4G LTE and NFC. What the extra £250 buys is Windows 11 Pro on an Intel Celeron N5100 with 8GB of RAM against the A8's 6GB, USB-A and HDMI ports, a fingerprint sensor, a MIL-STD-810G rating and the option of a built-in 2D barcode scanner. If everything you use runs in a web browser or has an Android app, most of that does not earn its money, and the A8 also gives you the brighter screen and the bigger battery for £250 less.

On the screen and battery, the A8 is ahead. Its screen is brighter at 1000 nits against 700, its 8000mAh battery is larger than the W8's 5000mAh and removable, so a charged spare takes over mid shift, and it has dual SIM 4G and VESA mount points. Its rear camera is 13MP with autofocus against 8MP, which counts if you photograph every job. The W8 has more listed on toughness: MIL-STD-810G and an operating range of -10°C to 50°C, where the A8 lists neither a MIL-STD rating nor an operating temperature. The W8 weighs 750g; the A8 does not list a weight. One more point: the A8 runs Android 12, an older version, so check that the apps you need support it.

Pay the £250 if even one program you rely on only installs on a Windows PC: manufacturer diagnostic or commissioning software, an older stock or accounts system, or a desktop package with no app. A cheaper tablet that cannot run that program is not cheaper at all. The W8 also has USB-A and HDMI for plugging into equipment or a screen, and the scanner version at £699, £70 over the standard W8, suits parts and asset scanning. Ask your software provider whether the specific apps you use run on the device before you order either, and try them on the device once it arrives. The five minute test in our Android or Windows guide is the place to start, and the field service page shows where each of the two fits that job.

Choose the Tuga A8 if

  • Everything you use runs in a web browser or has an Android app, so Windows would be £250 spent on nothing you need.
  • You read the screen outdoors: the A8 is brighter at 1000 nits against the W8's 700.
  • You want the larger battery and the option of a spare: 8000mAh and removable, against the W8's 5000mAh.
  • You want it docked in the van: the A8 has VESA mount points and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) is listed for both.
  • You photograph every job: a 13MP autofocus rear camera with flash against 8MP on the W8.

Choose the Tuga W8 if

  • One program you rely on only installs on a Windows PC, which settles it on its own.
  • You plug into equipment or a screen: the W8 has USB-C, USB-A and HDMI, where the A8 has USB-C, a DC input and pogo pin contacts.
  • You want a fingerprint sensor for sign-in: the W8 has one built in.
  • You want a listed rugged rating beyond IP67: the W8 lists MIL-STD-810G and -10°C to 50°C, the A8 lists neither.
  • You scan barcodes all day: the W8 with 2D Scanner is £699, £70 over the standard W8, and there is no scanner version of the A8.

What is different

Every line comes from the two specification sheets, the same figures as the product pages. Rows where the A8 and W8 differ are tinted.

  • The A8 is brighter: 1000 nits against 700 nits on the W8.

Identical on both: resolution (1280 x 800), IP rating (IP67).

FAQ

Questions about the A8 and W8

Only if you need Windows, or one of the W8's extras such as USB-A, HDMI output or the fingerprint sensor. The W8 costs £629 and the A8 £379. They share the same 8 inch size, 1280 x 800 resolution, 128GB of storage, IP67 sealing and 4G LTE, and the A8 has the brighter screen and the bigger, removable battery. The £250 buys Windows 11 Pro, 8GB of RAM against 6GB, USB-A and HDMI, a fingerprint sensor, MIL-STD-810G and the option of a scanner. If none of those is on your list, buy the Tuga A8. Both have the 12 month warranty included, there is no VAT to add to either price, and delivery is free to UK addresses in 7 to 10 working days.

Check before you buy rather than assuming. Anything that runs in a web browser or has an Android app is a candidate, but try the specific app on the device, or ask the software provider, before you rely on it. The A8 runs Android 12, which is older than the Android versions on the A6 and A10, so some apps may need a newer version; check the minimum each app asks for. Software that has to be installed on a Windows PC cannot be installed on the A8 at all; that is the clearest case where the Tuga W8 is the only choice of the two. Our Android or Windows guide has a five minute test for working out which camp you are in.

The A8 carries an 8000mAh battery and the W8 5000mAh, so the A8 starts the day with 60 percent more capacity, and its battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over. The W8 lists fast charging; the A8 does not. Both take the 12V DC Car Charger (£26), and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) charges either through its DC power input. The Charging Dock (£49.99) is listed for the W8 but not the A8; see accessories. The W8 is rated from -10°C to 50°C; the A8 lists no operating temperature. Our guide to rugged tablets in cold weather explains what the cold does to any battery.

No. The only Android device in the range with a built-in scanner is the Tuga A6 handheld (£349), which has a Zebra 2D scan engine; the scanner versions of the tablets are on the Windows models. The Tuga W8 with 2D Scanner costs £699, £70 more than the standard W8, and is sold from the same W8 product page. On the A8 you would scan with the camera through an app, or pair a separate scanner, and you should check that the app or scanner works on the device before relying on it. For occasional scanning a camera app may be enough; our guide to built-in barcode scanners covers when the extra cost pays off.
